html:
The Free State-Basotho wars were three wars fought between 1858 and 1868 by the Basotho of Moshoeshoe I and the Boer republic of the Orange Free State, over the fertile farmland west of the Caledon river.

Boer farmers moving north in the Great Trek settled on land the Basotho claimed. The Basotho held off the first attack, but in the war of 1865 to 1868 the Free State took much of their crop land and besieged Thaba Bosiu.

To save his people, Moshoeshoe asked Britain for protection, and in 1868 Basutoland became British. The land lost west of the river, still called the Conquered Territory, became part of the Free State, and modern Lesotho was left with mostly mountains.
